chapters.title: Ammon, Moab, Edom and the Philistines
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 25

Ammon

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, set your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

3Say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you said, 'Aha!' over My sanctuary when it was profaned, and over the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and over the house of Judah when they went into exile,

4therefore I am about to give you to the people of the east as a possession. They will set up their camps among you and pitch their tents among you; they will eat your fruit and drink your milk.

5I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks; and you will know that I am the LORD.

6For this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the contempt of your soul over the land of Israel,

7therefore I have stretched out My hand against you; I will give you as plunder to the nations, cut you off from the peoples and make you perish from the countries. I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the LORD.

Moab

8This is what the Lord GOD says: Because Moab and Seir said, 'The house of Judah is like all the nations,'

9therefore I am about to lay open the flank of Moab, stripping it of its cities, its cities on every side, the glory of the land, Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and Kiriathaim.

10To the people of the east I will give it as a possession, along with the Ammonites, so that the Ammonites will not be remembered among the nations,

11and I will carry out judgments on Moab; and they will know that I am the LORD.

Edom

12This is what the Lord GOD says: Because Edom took revenge on the house of Judah and has incurred great guilt by taking vengeance on them,

13therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will stretch out My hand against Edom and cut off from it human and beast, and I will make it a ruin; from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword.

14I will lay My vengeance on Edom by the hand of My people Israel, and they will deal with Edom according to My anger and My wrath; and they will know My vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.

The Philistines

15This is what the Lord GOD says: Because the Philistines acted in revenge and took vengeance with contempt of soul, to destroy, in never-ending hostility,

16therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to stretch out My hand against the Philistines; I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the remnant of the seacoast.

17I will carry out great vengeance on them with furious rebukes; and they will know that I am the LORD, when I lay My vengeance on them."

Notes

  • vv1–17 the nations — the book turns from Jerusalem to its neighbors, and chapters 25–32 hold the oracles against the nations. The first four are the peoples around Judah, each judged for what it did or said when Jerusalem fell.

  • v3 "Because you said, 'Aha!'" — he'ach, a cry of glee. Tyre says the same word over Jerusalem in 26:2. The charge against Ammon is not that it attacked, but that it was glad.

  • v8 "The house of Judah is like all the nations" — Moab's words deny the one thing that set Israel apart, what Moses asked for at Sinai: so that we are marked out, I and Your people, from every people on the face of the ground (Exodus 33:16).

  • vv12–14 "Because Edom took revenge on the house of Judah" — Edom's part in the fall is remembered elsewhere: Remember, LORD, against the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem (Psalm 137:7), and Lamentations turns to her, Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom… To you also the cup will pass (Lamentations 4:21). Has incurred great guilt, va-ye'shemu ashom, the verb with its own noun.

  • v16 "I will cut off the Cherethites" — ve-hikhratti et keretim, a play on sounds: karat, "cut off," and Keretim, a people of the Philistine coast.

  • vv5, 7, 11, 14, 17 "you will know that I am the LORD" — the sentence of Ezekiel's oracles against Israel, now said of the nations. Each judgment ends with the knowledge of who has spoken.

chapters.title: Tyre, a Bare Rock
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 26

1And it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem, 'Aha! The gate of the peoples is broken; it has swung open to me. I will be filled, now that she is laid waste,'

3therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring up many nations against you, as the sea brings up its waves.

4They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers; I will scrape her soil from her and make her a bare rock.

5She will be a place for spreading nets in the middle of the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD; and she will become plunder for the nations.

6Her daughters on the mainland will be killed by the sword; and they will know that I am the LORD.

7For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and chariots and horsemen, and a great company and army.

8Your daughters on the mainland he will kill with the sword. He will build a siege wall against you, heap up a ramp against you and raise a shield against you.

9He will set the blows of his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his axes.

10His horses are so many that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of horsemen, wheels and chariots, when he enters your gates as men enter a city that has been breached.

11With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will fall to the ground.

12They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise; they will break down your walls and destroy your fine houses, and your stones and your timber and your soil they will throw into the water.

13I will put an end to the noise of your songs, and the sound of your lyres will be heard no more.

14I will make you a bare rock; you will be a place for spreading nets; you will never be rebuilt, for I, the LORD, have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.

15This is what the Lord GOD says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan, when slaughter is done in your midst?

16Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, take off their robes and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling; they will sit on the ground and tremble every moment, and be appalled at you.

17They will take up a lament over you and say to you:
How you have perished,
you who were inhabited from the seas,
the city that was praised,
which was mighty on the sea,
she and those who lived in her,
who laid their terror on all who lived there!

18Now the coastlands tremble
on the day of your fall;
the coastlands by the sea
are dismayed at your passing.

19For this is what the Lord GOD says: When I make you a ruined city, like cities that are not inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the great waters cover you,

20then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old, and make you live in the lowest parts of the earth, among ruins from of old, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I will set glory in the land of the living.

21I will make you a terror, and you will be no more; though you are sought, you will never be found again, declares the Lord GOD."

Notes

  • v1 "in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month" — the Hebrew gives the day but not the month; the Greek is the same. Jerusalem fell in the eleventh year of Zedekiah (Jeremiah 39:2), whose reign began with the exile of Jehoiachin that Ezekiel counts by.

  • v2 "Aha! The gate of the peoples is broken; it has swung open to me" — Tyre's word is Ammon's, Aha! (25:3). Jerusalem is pictured as a gate through which the peoples passed; Tyre expects what went through it to come her way: I will be filled.

  • vv4, 14 "I will scrape her soil from her and make her a bare rock" — tsechiach sela, the words of 24:7–8, where Jerusalem left blood on the bare rock. Tsor, "Tyre," sounds like tsur, "rock": the city will be left a rock with nothing on it.

  • vv5, 14 "a place for spreading nets in the middle of the sea" — in the middle of the sea, as the city stood. The great trading city is to be no more than a place where fishermen dry their nets.

  • v7 "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings" — named here for the first time in the book. The book itself returns to the siege of Tyre later and says that Nebuchadnezzar's army labored hard against it and got no wages from it (29:17–18).

  • vv16–18 "all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones… They will take up a lament" — the other kings of the coast mourn as the people of chapter 24 were told not to: stripped of their robes, sitting on the ground.

  • vv19–21 "I will bring up the deep over you… with those who go down to the pit, to the people of old" — tehom, the deep of Genesis 1:2. The sea that made Tyre rich covers it, and it goes down to the pit, the place of the dead, the people of old.

chapters.title: The Ship Tyre
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 27

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"As for you, son of man, take up a lament over Tyre,

3and say to Tyre, you who dwell at the entrances to the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands: This is what the Lord GOD says:
Tyre, you have said,
'I am perfect in beauty.'

4Your borders are in the heart of the seas;
your builders made your beauty perfect.

5They made all your planks
of fir from Senir;
they took a cedar from Lebanon
to make a mast for you.

6Of oaks from Bashan
they made your oars;
your deck they made of ivory set in cypress
from the coastlands of Kittim.

7Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt
was your sail,
to be your banner;
blue and purple from the coastlands of Elishah
was your awning.

8The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad
were your rowers;
your skilled men, Tyre, were in you;
they were your sailors.

9The elders of Gebal and her skilled men were in you,
caulking your seams;
all the ships of the sea and their mariners were in you
to trade for your goods.

10Persia and Lud and Put
were in your army,
your men of war;
they hung shield and helmet in you;

were on your walls all around,

20Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.

21Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were the merchants under your hand; in lambs, rams and goats they traded with you.

22The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; the best of all spices, every precious stone and gold they gave for your wares.

23Haran, Canneh and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad traded with you.

24They traded with you in choice garments, in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in carpets of many colors, bound with cords and firmly made, in your marketplace.

25The ships of Tarshish
carried your merchandise;
so you were filled and very heavy
in the heart of the seas.

26Your rowers have brought you
out into the great waters;
the east wind has broken you
in the heart of the seas.

27Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise,
your mariners and your sailors,
your caulkers, your dealers in merchandise,
and all your men of war who are in you,
with all your company that is in your midst,
will fall into the heart of the seas
on the day of your fall.

the shores will shake.

29All who handle the oar,
the mariners and all the sailors of the sea,
will come down from their ships
and stand on the land.

30They will raise their voices over you
and cry out bitterly;
they will throw dust on their heads
and roll in ashes.

31They will make themselves bald for you
and put on sackcloth,
and weep over you in bitterness of soul
with bitter mourning.

32In their wailing they will take up a lament for you
and lament over you:
'Who is like Tyre,
like one silenced in the middle of the sea?'

33When your wares went out from the seas,
you satisfied many peoples;
with the abundance of your wealth and your merchandise
you made the kings of the earth rich.

34Now you are broken by the seas,
in the depths of the waters;
your merchandise and all your company
have fallen with you.

35All the inhabitants of the coastlands
are appalled at you;
their kings shudder with horror;
their faces are troubled.

36The merchants among the peoples hiss at you;
you have become a terror
and will be no more forever."

Notes

  • vv3–11 "Tyre, you have said, 'I am perfect in beauty'… your builders made your beauty perfect" — the lament pictures the city as a ship, built of the best the world could give: fir from Senir (Mount Hermon), cedar from Lebanon, oaks from Bashan, linen from Egypt, and crewed and guarded by the peoples of the coast. Perfect in beauty, kelilat yofi, comes back at 28:12, said of Tyre's king.

  • vv12–24 the traders — a list of the known world, many of its names from the table of nations: Javan and Tubal and Meshech (Genesis 10:2), Togarmah (10:3), Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim (10:4), Sheba and Dedan (10:7). Tyre's goods reach from Tarshish in the west to Sheba in the south and Asshur in the east.

  • v13 "human beings and vessels of bronze" — nefesh adam, "souls of men," traded beside bronze pots: slaves.

  • v17 "Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; wheat of Minnith, pannag, honey, oil and balm" — Israel's farm goods, some of them the gifts Jacob sent to Egypt, a little balm and a little honey (Genesis 43:11). Pannag is found only here, and what it was is not known; the Greek has perfumes and cassia.

  • v19 "Vedan and Javan from Uzal" — the Hebrew of the opening words is uncertain; Uzal is named among the sons of Joktan (Genesis 10:27).

  • v26 "the east wind has broken you in the heart of the seas" — the ship, loaded so heavy that it rides low, is wrecked by the wind that dried up the vine of 17:10 and 19:12.

  • vv28–36 "At the sound of your sailors' cry the shores will shake… Who is like Tyre?" — the sailors who survive come ashore and mourn as for the dead: dust, ashes, shaved heads, sackcloth. Who is like Tyre? echoes the praise of God, Who is like You among the gods, LORD? (Exodus 15:11), now said of a sunken ship.

  • v36 "you have become a terror and will be no more forever" — the refrain that ends each Tyre oracle (26:21; 27:36; 28:19).

chapters.title: The King of Tyre in Eden
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 28

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because your heart is proud and you have said, 'I am a god; I sit in the seat of gods in the heart of the seas,' yet you are a man and not a god, though you make your heart like the heart of a god —

3you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you;

4by your wisdom and your understanding you have gained wealth for yourself and gathered gold and silver into your treasuries;

5by your great wisdom in trade you have increased your wealth, and your heart has grown proud because of your wealth —

6therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you make your heart like the heart of a god,

7therefore I am about to bring strangers against you, the most ruthless of nations; they will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and profane your splendor.

8They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.

9Will you still say, 'I am a god,' before those who kill you, when you are a man and not a god in the hands of those who wound you?

10You will die the death of the uncircumcised by the hands of strangers, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD."

A Lament for the King of Tyre

11The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

12"Son of man, take up a lament over the king of Tyre and say to him: This is what the Lord GOD says:
You were the seal of perfection,
full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

13You were in Eden, the garden of God;
every precious stone was your covering:
carnelian, topaz and diamond,
beryl, onyx and jasper,
sapphire, turquoise and emerald;
and of gold was the work of your settings and your sockets in you;
on the day you were created they were prepared.

14You were an anointed cherub, the one who shelters;
I set you there.
You were on the holy mountain of God;
you walked among the stones of fire.

15You were blameless in your ways
from the day you were created,
until wrongdoing was found in you.

16Through the abundance of your trade
your inside was filled with violence,
and you sinned;
so I cast you out as profane from the mountain of God,
and I destroyed you, sheltering cherub,
from among the stones of fire.

17Your heart was proud because of your beauty;
you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor.
I threw you to the ground;
I set you before kings
for them to look at you.

18By the multitude of your iniquities,
in the dishonesty of your trade,
you profaned your sanctuaries;
so I brought fire out from your midst;
it consumed you,
and I turned you to ashes on the earth
in the sight of all who saw you.

19All who know you among the peoples
are appalled at you;
you have become a terror
and will be no more forever."

Sidon, and Israel Gathered

20The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

21"Son of man, set your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her,

22and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst. They will know that I am the LORD, when I carry out judgments in her and show Myself holy in her.

23I will send pestilence into her and blood into her streets; the slain will fall in her midst by the sword that is against her on every side; and they will know that I am the LORD.

24No more will there be for the house of Israel a pricking brier or a painful thorn among all around them who treat them with contempt; and they will know that I am the Lord GOD.

25This is what the Lord GOD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and show Myself holy among them in the sight of the nations, they will live in their own land that I gave to My servant Jacob.

26They will live in it securely; they will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live securely when I carry out judgments on all around them who treat them with contempt; and they will know that I am the LORD their God."

Notes

  • vv2, 9 "I am a god… yet you are a man and not a god" — el ani… ve-attah adam ve-lo el. The boast of the king of Babylon in Isaiah, I will make myself like the Most High (Isaiah 14:14), now in the mouth of Tyre's ruler, and answered in the same words twice: a man and not a god.

  • v3 "you are wiser than Daniel" — the name is written Dan'el and read Daniel, as at 14:14, 20. The Greek makes it a question, Are you wiser than Daniel?

  • vv12–13 "You were the seal of perfection… You were in Eden, the garden of God" — the lament moves the king into the first garden. Perfect in beauty was Tyre's own boast (27:3).

  • v13 "carnelian, topaz and diamond, beryl, onyx and jasper, sapphire, turquoise and emerald" — nine of the twelve stones of the high priest's breastpiece, in Exodus's names (Exodus 28:17–20); the third row, jacinth, agate and amethyst, is missing. The Greek lists all twelve. Your settings and your sockets, tuppekha u-neqavekha, is uncertain: the words can also mean "your tambourines and your pipes."

  • vv14, 16 "You were an anointed cherub, the one who shelters… I destroyed you, sheltering cherub" — at keruv, "you, a cherub," as the Hebrew is pointed. The Greek reads the same letters as et keruv, "with the cherub": from the day you were created you were with the cherub, and in v16, the cherub drove you out from among the stones of fire. Who shelters, ha-sokhekh, is the word of the cherubim over the ark, sheltering the cover with their wings (Exodus 25:20).

  • v16 "so I cast you out as profane from the mountain of God" — the story of Eden: He drove the human out, and He made dwell east of the garden of Eden the cherubim (Genesis 3:24). Wealth from trade is what filled the king with violence, the charge Tyre's whole lament has prepared.

  • v24 "a pricking brier or a painful thorn" — the law's warning about the peoples left in the land, barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides (Numbers 33:55). With the neighbors judged, the thorn is removed.

  • vv25–26 "they will build houses and plant vineyards" — what Jeremiah told the exiles to do in Babylon, Build houses and live in them (Jeremiah 29:5), promised now in their own land.

chapters.title: The Monster in the Nile
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 29

1In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

3Speak and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great monster lying among his streams, who has said, 'My Nile is my own; I made it for myself.'

4I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your streams stick to your scales. I will haul you up from among your streams, with all the fish of your streams sticking to your scales.

5I will fling you into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your streams. You will fall on the open field, and no one will gather you up or collect you. I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the heavens.

6All who live in Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.

7When they took hold of you with the hand, you splintered and tore open every shoulder; when they leaned on you, you broke and crushed all their loins.

8Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will cut off man and beast from you.

9The land of Egypt will become a desolation and a ruin, and they will know that I am the LORD. Because he said, 'The Nile is mine; I made it,'

10therefore I am against you and against your streams, and I will make the land of Egypt an utter ruin and a desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.

11No foot of man will pass through it, and no foot of beast will pass through it, and no one will live in it for forty years.

12I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities will be a desolation among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries.

13For this is what the Lord GOD says: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.

14I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.

15It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and will never again lift itself up over the nations. I will make them so few that they will not rule over the nations.

16It will never again be the confidence of the house of Israel, bringing their iniquity to remembrance when they turn to them for help; and they will know that I am the Lord GOD."

Egypt, the Wages for Tyre

17And it came to pass in the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

18"Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon worked his army hard against Tyre; every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder worn raw. Yet he and his army got no wages from Tyre for the work he did against it.

19Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its multitude, take its spoil and seize its plunder, and it will be the wages for his army.

20As the pay for his labor I have given him the land of Egypt, because they acted for Me, declares the Lord GOD.

21On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth among them; and they will know that I am the LORD."

Notes

  • v1 "In the tenth year" — counted from King Jehoiachin's exile (1:2). The oracle is dated a year before the Tyre oracle of 26:1, the eleventh year: the oracles against the nations are grouped by nation, not by date. The Greek dates it the twelfth year… on the first of the month.

  • v3 "the great monster" — ha-tannim ha-gadol, the word of the great sea-monsters God created on the fifth day (Genesis 1:21), and of Aaron's staff, which will become a serpent, a tannin, before Pharaoh (Exodus 7:9). Now Pharaoh is the monster, lying in the Nile, and the LORD hauls him out with hooks like a fish.

  • vv3, 9 "My Nile is my own; I made it for myself… The Nile is mine; I made it" — v3's verb is asitini, made with the ending me. It can be I made it for myself, the boast of v9 with for myself added, or I made myself: Pharaoh claiming to be his own maker, as the ruler of Tyre claimed I am a god (28:2). v9 repeats the boast without the ending. The Greek has The rivers are mine, and I made them.

  • vv6–7 "a staff of reed" — the picture the Assyrian envoy used to Hezekiah: the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt, which will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it (2 Kings 18:21; Isaiah 36:6). Judah's king turned to Egypt against Babylon as well (17:15), and Pharaoh did not help him (17:17).

  • v7 "you broke and crushed all their loins" — the Hebrew has ve-ha'amadta lahem kol motnayim, you made all their loins stand, which leaves the second line without the injury the first has (tore open every shoulder). The rendering follows the Greek, you broke all their loins.

  • v10 "from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush" — the whole land, end to end, out to Syene on the border of Cush. Migdol is also named among the camps before the sea (Exodus 14:2). The Greek has the borders of the Ethiopians, its name for Cush.

  • v14 "the land of Pathros, the land of their origin" — Isaiah lists Pathros between Egypt and Cush (Isaiah 11:11), and the table of nations names the Pathrusim among the sons of Egypt (Genesis 10:14).

  • v16 "bringing their iniquity to remembrance" — mazkir avon, the phrase of 21:23, he brings their iniquity to remembrance. Egypt as Israel's confidence kept that iniquity in view, the trust Isaiah condemned: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help (Isaiah 31:1).

  • vv17–18 "in the twenty-seventh year… no wages from Tyre" — the latest date in the book, sixteen years after the Tyre oracles of chapter 26. The book keeps the oracle that Nebuchadnezzar would come against Tyre (26:7) and records here that his army got nothing for its labor. Egypt is given as its pay, because they acted for Me: Jeremiah calls him Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, My servant (Jeremiah 25:9).

  • v21 "I will make a horn sprout… I will open your mouth among them" — atsmiach qeren, the words of Psalm 132:17, There I will make a horn sprout for David. Pitchon peh, an opening of the mouth: the prophet had been told he would be mute until a fugitive came with the news (24:26): On that day your mouth will be opened (24:27).

chapters.title: The Day of Egypt, and Pharaoh's Broken Arm
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 30

1The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Wail, 'Alas for the day!'

3For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near; a day of cloud, it will be the time of the nations.

4A sword will come against Egypt, and anguish will be in Cush, when the slain fall in Egypt, and her multitude is taken away and her foundations are torn down.

5Cush and Put and Lud, all the mixed peoples and Cub, and the people of the land of the covenant will fall with them by the sword.

6This is what the LORD says: Those who support Egypt will fall, and the pride of her strength will come down. From Migdol to Syene they will fall in her by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.

7They will be desolate among desolate lands, and her cities will lie among ruined cities.

8They will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all her helpers are broken.

9On that day messengers will go out from Me in ships to terrify Cush in her security, and anguish will come on them on the day of Egypt; for it is coming.

10This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to the multitude of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.

11He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land; they will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.

12I will make the streams dry ground and sell the land into the hand of evil men; I will make the land and all that fills it desolate by the hand of strangers. I, the LORD, have spoken.

13This is what the Lord GOD says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the worthless gods in Memphis. There will no longer be a prince from the land of Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.

14I will make Pathros desolate, set fire to Zoan, and carry out judgments on No.

15I will pour out My wrath on Sin, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the multitude of No.

16I will set fire to Egypt; Sin will writhe in anguish, No will be broken open, and Memphis will face foes by day.

17The young men of Aven and of Pi-beseth will fall by the sword, and the cities themselves will go into captivity.

18At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark, when I break there the yoke bars of Egypt and the pride of her strength comes to an end in her. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.

19So I will carry out judgments on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD."

The Broken Arm

20And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

21"Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it has not been bound up to heal it, nor a bandage put on to bind it and make it strong enough to hold a sword.

22Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break his arms, both the strong one and the broken one, and make the sword fall from his hand.

23I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries.

24I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and he will groan before him like a man mortally wounded.

25I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall; and they will know that I am the LORD, when I put My sword into the hand of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.

26I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the countries; and they will know that I am the LORD."

Notes

  • vv2–3 "Wail, 'Alas for the day!' For the day is near, the day of the LORD is near" — the cry Isaiah raised over Babylon, Wail, for the day of the LORD is near (Isaiah 13:6), and that Ezekiel raised over Israel's land, the day is near (7:7). The day that came on Jerusalem now comes on Egypt.

  • v5 "Cush and Put and Lud, all the mixed peoples and Cub" — Egypt's allies and soldiers; Put and Lud served in Tyre's army too (27:10). Kuv is found only here, and no one knows who they were. The Greek list differs: Persians and Cretans and Lydians and Libyans.

  • v5 "the people of the land of the covenant" — benei erets ha-berit. It can mean the people of Egypt's allied lands, the land of the treaty, or the people of the covenant itself: Judeans who had gone down to Egypt (Jeremiah 43:7). The Greek has the sons of My covenant.

  • v9 "messengers will go out from Me in ships to terrify Cush" — Isaiah pictured Cush as the land which sends envoys by the sea, in vessels of papyrus on the waters (Isaiah 18:2). Here the messengers go the other way, from the LORD to Cush, to terrify it with the day of Egypt.

  • v13 "the idols… the worthless gods" — gillulim, Ezekiel's word for idols throughout the book, and elilim, nothings, the word Isaiah used of Egypt's gods, the idols of Egypt tremble before Him (Isaiah 19:1). The Greek has nobles and rulers instead of idols and gods.

  • vv13–18 the cities of Egypt — the Greek gives them the names its own readers knew: Memphis (Noph), Tanis (Zoan), Diospolis (No, called Amon of No in Jeremiah 46:25), Sais (Sin), Heliopolis (Aven), Bubastis (Pi-beseth) and Taphnai (Tahpanhes, spelled Tehaphnehes in this verse).

  • v17 "Aven" — the city called On in Joseph's story (Genesis 41:45), with the same letters pointed aven, trouble or wickedness.

  • v18 "the day will grow dark" — the Leningrad Codex points the verb chasakh, held back: the day will be held back. With the other dot on the same letter it is chashakh, grow dark, which the Greek has and the cloud of the same verse supports.

  • v18 "when I break there the yoke bars of Egypt" — the words of the Exodus: I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright (Leviticus 26:13). Now the LORD breaks Egypt's own yoke bars, in Egypt. The Greek reads the scepters of Egypt.

  • vv21–25 "the arm of Pharaoh… the arms of the king of Babylon" — the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt with an outstretched arm (Exodus 6:6). Now He breaks Pharaoh's arm and strengthens Babylon's, and puts His own sword in Babylon's hand.

chapters.title: The Great Cedar
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 31

1And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?

3Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon,
fair in its branches, a thicket of shade,
and tall in stature;
its crown rose among the thick branches.

4The waters made it grow;
the deep made it tall,
running its rivers around the place where it was planted
and sending out its channels to all the trees of the field.

5So it grew taller
than all the trees of the field;
its boughs multiplied, and its branches grew long
from the abundant water as it spread them out.

6In its boughs
all the birds of the heavens made their nests;
under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth,
and all great nations lived in its shade.

7It was beautiful in its greatness,
in the length of its branches,
for its roots went down to abundant waters.

8The cedars in the garden of God could not overshadow it;
the firs were not like its boughs,
and the plane trees were nothing beside its branches;
no tree in the garden of God
was like it in its beauty.

9I made it beautiful
with its many branches,
and all the trees of Eden
that were in the garden of God envied it.

10Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you were so tall in stature, and it set its crown among the thick branches, and its heart grew proud of its height,

11I gave it into the hand of the mighty one of the nations, and he dealt with it; for its wickedness I drove it out.

12Strangers, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it lying. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys, and its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth came down from its shade and left it.

13On its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens settle, and among its boughs are all the beasts of the field,

14so that no trees by the waters may grow tall in their stature or set their crowns among the thick branches, and no tree that drinks water may rise up to them in its height. For they are all given over to death, to the lowest parts of the earth, among the sons of men, with those who go down to the pit.

15This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day it went down to Sheol I brought mourning; I covered the deep over it, I held back its rivers, and the great waters were stopped. I clothed Lebanon in gloom for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.

16I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit; and all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the lowest parts of the earth.

17They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword, and so did those who were its arm, who had lived in its shade among the nations.

18Whom are you like, in glory and in greatness, among the trees of Eden? You will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lowest parts of the earth; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD."

Notes

  • vv2, 18 "Whom are you like in your greatness?… This is Pharaoh and all his multitude" — the chapter is one question, a parable and its answer. Hamon, multitude, is Egypt's word in these oracles (29:19; 30:4, 10, 15): its crowds, its armies, its pomp. Chapter 32 says it over Egypt's dead.

  • v3 "Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon" — Pharaoh is shown Assyria, the empire that fell before him, and Isaiah had already pictured its fall as a forest cut down: Lebanon will fall by the Majestic One (Isaiah 10:34). The Greek also has Assur, and calls the tree a cypress.

  • vv3, 10, 14 "among the thick branches" — bein avotim, the words used of the vine in the lament of 19:11, Its height towered among the thick branches. The Greek reads among the clouds.

  • v4 "the deep made it tall" — tehom, the deep of creation (Genesis 1:2). In v15 the same deep is covered over the fallen tree, and its rivers are held back.

  • vv6, 13 "all the birds of the heavens made their nests" — the picture of Ezekiel's own cedar, the one the LORD plants on the mountain of Israel: Under it will live every bird of every wing (17:23). Jesus uses it for the kingdom, the mustard seed that becomes a tree so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches (Matthew 13:32). Fallen, this tree is only a perch.

  • vv8–9, 16, 18 "the garden of God… the trees of Eden" — the garden where the king of Tyre was set (28:13). Here its trees envy the cedar, and in the end go down to the dead with it.

  • v10 "Because you were so tall… and it set its crown" — the Hebrew moves from you to it inside one sentence. The tree is Assyria; the one being spoken to is Pharaoh.

  • v11 "I drove it out" — gerashtihu, the verb of Eden: He drove the human out (Genesis 3:24). The mighty one of the nations, el goyim, is unnamed; 30:24–25 has given the sword to the king of Babylon.

  • vv15–16 "were comforted in the lowest parts of the earth" — the trees already among the dead take comfort that the greatest of them has come down too, as in Isaiah's song over the king of Babylon: Even the cypresses rejoice over you, the cedars of Lebanon (Isaiah 14:8).

  • v17 "those who were its arm" — zero'o, its arm: its allies, with the word of 30:21–25. The same letters read zar'o, its seed, which the Greek has.

chapters.title: A Lament for Pharaoh, and the Nations in the Pit
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 32

1And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

2"Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him:
You thought yourself a young lion of the nations,
but you are like the monster in the seas;
you burst out in your rivers,
muddied the water with your feet
and fouled their rivers.

3This is what the Lord GOD says:
I will spread My net over you
with a company of many peoples,
and they will haul you up in My dragnet.

4I will fling you on the land;
I will hurl you onto the open field.
I will make all the birds of the heavens settle on you,
and fill the beasts of the whole earth with you.

5I will lay your flesh on the mountains
and fill the valleys with your carcass.

6I will drench the land with your flowing blood,
up to the mountains,
and the ravines will be full of you.

7When I snuff you out, I will cover the heavens
and darken their stars;
I will cover the sun with a cloud,
and the moon will not give its light.

8I will darken over you
all the shining lamps in the heavens,
and put darkness on your land,
declares the Lord GOD.

9I will trouble the hearts of many peoples
when I bring your ruin among the nations,
to lands you have not known.

10I will make many peoples appalled at you,
and their kings will shudder with horror over you
when I brandish My sword before them;
they will tremble every moment,
each for his own life,
on the day of your fall.

11For this is what the Lord GOD says:
The sword of the king of Babylon
will come upon you.

12By the swords of mighty ones
I will make your multitude fall,
all of them the most ruthless of nations.
They will bring the pride of Egypt to ruin,
and all her multitude will be destroyed.

13I will destroy all her cattle
from beside the many waters;
no human foot will muddy them again,
nor will the hoofs of cattle muddy them.

14Then I will make their waters settle
and make their rivers run like oil,
declares the Lord GOD.

15When I make the land of Egypt a desolation,
a land stripped of all that fills it,
when I strike down all who live in it,
they will know that I am the LORD.

16This is a lament, and they will chant it;
the daughters of the nations will chant it;
over Egypt and all her multitude they will chant it,
declares the Lord GOD."

Down to the Pit

17And it came to pass in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth of the month, that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

18"Son of man, wail over the multitude of Egypt and bring them down, her and the daughters of majestic nations, to the lowest parts of the earth, with those who go down to the pit.

19Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down, and be laid with the uncircumcised!

20They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword has been given; drag her away, with all her multitude!

21The mightiest of the mighty ones will speak to him from the middle of Sheol, with his helpers: 'They have come down; they lie still, the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.'

22Assyria is there with all her company, her graves all around her, all of them slain, fallen by the sword,

23whose graves are set in the far reaches of the pit, and her company is around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who spread terror in the land of the living.

24Elam is there with all her multitude around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the lowest parts of the earth, who spread their terror in the land of the living; they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

25Among the slain they have made a bed for her with all her multitude, her graves all around her; all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, for their terror was spread in the land of the living, and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; she is laid among the slain.

26Meshech and Tubal are there with all her multitude, her graves all around her; all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, for they spread their terror in the land of the living.

27They do not lie with the mighty ones who fell long ago, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were laid under their heads and whose iniquities lay on their bones, for the terror of the mighty ones was in the land of the living.

28But you will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.

29Edom is there, her kings and all her princes, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword; they lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

30The chiefs of the north are there, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain, put to shame for all the terror their might inspired; they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

31Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude: Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.

32For I spread My terror in the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword: Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD."

Notes

  • v2 "You thought yourself a young lion of the nations" — kefir goyim nidmeita. Nidmeita can be you were likened, the verb of 31:2, 18, Whom are you like?, as the Greek takes it; or, from a second verb with the same letters, you are ruined, the word of Isaiah 6:5, Woe is me! For I am ruined. A lament could open either way: Young lion of the nations, you are ruined. The monster is the tannim of 29:3.

  • v5 "your carcass" — ramutekha, a word found only here. It seems to come from rum, to be high: the great body heaped up in the valleys. The Greek has your blood.

  • vv7–8 "When I snuff you out, I will cover the heavens… and put darkness on your land" — the ninth plague again, darkness over the land of Egypt (Exodus 10:21), now as the end of Pharaoh's light. The shining lamps in the heavens, me'orei or, are the lamps of the fourth day (Genesis 1:14). The darkened sun and moon return in Isaiah 13:10 and in Jesus' words about the end: the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light (Matthew 24:29).

  • vv12, 21, 27 "mighty ones" — gibborim, warriors. The Greek renders the word gigantes, giants, all three times, as it renders the mighty ones who were of old in Genesis 6:4: the giants who were from of old.

  • v17 "in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth of the month" — the Hebrew gives no month. The Greek has the first month.

  • vv18–32 the nations in the pit — Assyria, Elam, Meshech and Tubal, Edom, the chiefs of the north and the Sidonians, each laid with its multitude and its graves around it. The powers that spread terror in the land of the living lie in the far reaches of the pit, the place Isaiah gave the king of Babylon (Isaiah 14:15). Meshech and Tubal were Tyre's traders (27:13).

  • v27 "They do not lie with the mighty ones who fell long ago" — the Hebrew has nofelim me-arelim, fallen ones of the uncircumcised. The rendering follows the Greek, which reads me-olam, from of old: the giants who fell from of old, the words of Genesis 6:4, the mighty ones who were of old; the pit already holds the people of old (26:20). They were buried as warriors, with their weapons and their swords under their heads, and Meshech and Tubal are not laid with them. The Greek has no not: in it, they lie together.

  • v31 "Pharaoh will see them and be comforted" — ve-nicham, the comfort of the fallen trees in 31:16: that he is not alone among the dead.

  • v32 "For I spread My terror" — the written text has chittito, his terror, which the Greek also has; the reading tradition, followed here, has chittiti, My terror.

But you will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.
Edom is there, her kings and all her princes, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword; they lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

The chiefs of the north are there, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain, put to shame for all the terror their might inspired; they lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude: Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
For I spread My terror in the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword: Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD."
